title: A Pointwise Elementary Logarithmic Lower Bound on π
description: Upgrades the parent's powers-of-two bound π(2^k) ≥ k to a bound valid at every natural number: π(n) ≥ ⌊log₂ n⌋, via monotonicity of π and 2^⌊log₂ n⌋ ≤ n. Records the counting-side dual of the already-formalized ceiling on the k-th prime pₖ ≤ 2^(k+1), so both elementary directions of the Bertrand bridge sit together. Deliberately weaker than the gallery's Chebyshev Θ(x/log x) bound — its value is being a clean, pointwise, fully elementary estimate from Bertrand alone. 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: Bertrand's postulate — a prime in (n, 2n] for every n — was conjectured by Bertrand (1845), first proved by Chebyshev (1852), and given an elementary binomial-coefficient proof by Erdős (1932). Beyond guaranteeing a prime in each doubling interval, it yields two dual quantitative facts by pure iteration: a lower bound on how many primes lie below x, and an upper bound on how large the n-th prime can be. The parent entry recorded the first at powers of two (π(2^k) ≥ k); this follow-up makes it pointwise and pairs it with the dual.
overview.problemStatement: Extend the parent's powers-of-two lower bound π(2^k) ≥ k to a bound valid at every natural number, and connect it to the elementary ceiling on the size of the n-th prime.
overview.text: Proves π(n) ≥ ⌊log₂ n⌋ for all n and records the dual pₖ ≤ 2^(k+1).
overview.proofStrategy: For any n ≥ 1 set k = ⌊log₂ n⌋. Mathlib's Nat.pow_log_le_self gives 2^k ≤ n, so monotonicity of π yields π(n) ≥ π(2^k), and the parent's primeCounting_two_pow_ge gives π(2^k) ≥ k. Chaining these is the whole proof. The dual direction — the k-th prime is at most 2^(k+1) — is already formalized in PrimeGapBounds via Bertrand's pₖ₊₁ ≤ 2·pₖ, and is re-exported and read in log scale here.
keyInsights: Monotonicity of π plus 2^⌊log₂ n⌋ ≤ n instantly transports a bound known only at powers of two to every natural number — no new number theory is needed
π(n) ≥ ⌊log₂ n⌋ is the exact counting-side dual of the k-th-prime ceiling pₖ ≤ 2^(k+1): both are one-line iterations of Bertrand from opposite ends

The bound is honestly weaker than the Chebyshev Θ(n/log n) estimate already in the gallery; its interest is that it is fully elementary and pointwise, with no primorial factorization and no real-analytic error term
Evaluating ⌊log₂ n⌋ at concrete n (e.g. ⌊log₂ 1000⌋ = 9) via Nat.log_eq_of_pow_le_of_lt_pow turns the bound into explicit prime-count certificates
prerequisites: the integer logarithm Nat.log and its monotonicity

conclusion.summary: Fully verified (0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide) upgrade of the parent's powers-of-two bound to the pointwise estimate π(n) ≥ ⌊log₂ n⌋, paired with the elementary k-th-prime ceiling pₖ ≤ 2^(k+1). Together they bracket the primes from both sides using only Bertrand's postulate.
conclusion.implications: Monotonicity turns a sparse-sequence bound into a bound at every n, giving a clean elementary lower bound on the prime count and, dually, an exponential upper bound on the n-th prime — both far from the sharp PNT asymptotic but fully self-contained.
